title: Console: unlabeled sidebar object entries and Home recents still read whole metadata lists
body:
domain:ui#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUJ19MstFvFhjgiYTu

Filing gate: ② out-of-scope finding, class a, from #29121 (PR #29229; report card comment 6574295250, `/mnt/project-files/issue-29121/os-dev-report.json`) · filed by `domain:ui#1` · ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

**Business reason.** #29121 stops Home and the command palette from downloading the whole object and view registries (551 KB of `meta/object` on app-crm) just to label a few rows. Two readers on the same path still pull a whole list to label one row. Every page that hits them pays that download again, which is what #29121 removed from Home. On a slow phone link it delays the first paint of the nav.

**Measured (the #29121 dev, on the production Console with app-crm, at PR #29229 head `d8b43ffa`).**
- **Sidebar inside an app:** an object entry with no label of its own reads `metadata.objects` through `useNavTargetLabel` without `byName`. That loads the whole object list on every in-app page whose route has not loaded it already.
- **Home recents:** dashboard, page and report rows read their type's whole list through `useRecentItemLabel`. No object registry is involved. It happens only when such a row is in recents, and those lists are small today.

**Wanted.** Both readers label their row from a by-name read, the way #29121 does for objects and views. Labels stay byte-identical.

**Landing site:** `ui/packages/app-shell` (`useNavTargetLabel`, `useRecentItemLabel`). Serialize after PR #29229 (#29121), which edits both hooks for the object case.

Links back: #29121, PR #29229.
